title.en: One plan can reveal more than a general label
title.zh: 用一次安排看见具体协商

paragraphs.zh: 补充原创场景：两位虚构朋友想一起逛旧书摊，一人想慢慢挑书，另一人需要在半小时后离开。可以先确认可用时间，再决定共同逛哪一区。即使最后没有找到都喜欢的书，也可能已经把限制说清楚；反过来，买到同一本书也不证明双方都能提出条件。这里比较约定怎样形成，与共同爱好多少、由谁主动发消息不同。
paragraphs.en: In an additional original scene, two fictional friends visit a used-book stall. One wants to browse slowly; the other must leave after half an hour. They could clarify the available time before choosing a section to visit together. Finding no book both like does not undo a clearly discussed limit; buying the same book does not establish that both could state their conditions. This concerns how an agreement forms, rather than shared interests or who messages first.

title.zh: 尝试一次清楚且可拒绝的请求

paragraphs.zh: “这次见面对你最重要的是什么？我能留的时间是……，如果不够，我们可以怎样改？”对同一项虚构安排各列一个条件和一个可调整部分。可以找不到共同方案，不必用答应超出余力的要求来证明合拍。
paragraphs.en: “What matters most to you about this meeting? I can stay for …; how could we adjust if that is not enough?” List one condition and one adjustable part for each person in the fictional plan. There may be no shared solution, without accepting an unmanageable request to prove compatibility.

paragraphs.zh: 这些是可选的原创讨论素材，不是对朋友行为的核实报告。五组各四题分别汇总近期观察，不组成匹配百分比、朋友排名或人格类型；一项NA只使所属组保留资料不足，五份完整指南始终可读。可以只阅读或写不发送的句子，分享公开指南无需发送答卷、分数、聊天记录或他人身份。
paragraphs.en: These optional original discussion examples are not verified reports about a friend’s behaviour. Five groups of four separately summarise recent observations, without compatibility percentages, friend rankings or personality types. One NA withholds only its group, while all five complete guides remain readable. Reading or drafting an unsent sentence is enough; sharing the public guide requires no answers, scores, chat records or another person’s identity.

title.en: Clarify a changed plan before deciding what it means
title.zh: 先澄清改约，再判断它意味着什么

paragraphs.zh: 补充原创场景：两位虚构朋友讨论一张共同绘制的路线图。收到“这里不对”的短消息后，一人以为整张图被否定，问清才知道对方只是指出入口换了。澄清信息并不要求同意每条修改；认真听完也不意味着必须提供建议。这里关注能否说明、询问和表达需要，不用消息长短衡量共情，也不根据一次误会给朋友定型。
paragraphs.en: In an additional original scene, two fictional friends discuss a map they drew together. A brief message saying “this is wrong” seems to reject the whole map, until a question reveals that the entrance has changed. Clarifying does not require accepting every revision; listening does not require offering advice. Notice opportunities to explain, ask and state needs, without using message length as empathy or one misunderstanding as a label for the friend.

title.en: Choose one small request and a workable time
title.zh: 选一个小请求，再确认适合的时间

paragraphs.zh: “你说不对，是指入口还是整条路线？我想先听清具体位置，再讨论怎么改。”可以只为虚构消息写一个澄清问题和一个自己的感受，不猜对方动机。若对方现在不方便，是否再谈、何时再谈仍可商量。
paragraphs.en: “When you say it is wrong, do you mean the entrance or the whole route? I would like to understand the location before discussing changes.” Draft one clarification and one feeling for the fictional message without assigning a motive. Whether and when to return to it can be discussed if now is inconvenient.

title.en: A small plan can include unequal but agreed contributions
title.zh: 小安排可以容纳不一样的投入

paragraphs.zh: 补充原创场景：两位虚构朋友准备交换自制书签。一人提议周末见面，另一人说明可以带纸但不能裁切，双方再商量是否简化样式。提出见面、说明余力与答应承担任务是不同步骤；带纸不自动抵消未告知的失约，任务数量不相等也不说明贡献失衡。这里看参与如何被确认和调整，不是计算谁更珍惜友谊。
paragraphs.en: In an additional original scene, two fictional friends prepare to exchange handmade bookmarks. One suggests a weekend meeting; the other can bring paper but cannot cut it, so they discuss a simpler design. Suggesting contact, explaining capacity and accepting a task are different steps. Bringing paper does not automatically cancel an unexplained missed commitment; unequal task counts do not establish unequal contribution. This concerns confirming and adjusting participation, rather than measuring who values the friendship more.

paragraphs.zh: “我可以负责……，暂时做不到……；你愿意承担哪一部分，或者我们把活动缩小？”写明一项确实答应的事与一个变化时的沟通方式。邀请不是默认分工，感谢一次帮助也不把它变成长久义务。
paragraphs.en: “I can handle … and cannot currently do … . What would you want to take on, or should we make the activity smaller?” State one genuinely accepted task and how a change could be communicated. An invitation does not assign duties, and thanking one contribution does not make it permanent.

title.en: A quiet weekend can include a clear contact plan
title.zh: 安静的周末也可以有清楚的联系安排

paragraphs.zh: 补充原创场景：虚构的朋友聚会后，有人想把合照放进一个小群。愿意被拍、愿意让某位朋友留存，与愿意让群成员看到，是不同决定。即使平时经常互发照片，也应另问这张图和这个接收范围；有人不同意时，不需要从本组均分寻找覆盖这一回答的许可。这里关注具体选择，不规定朋友必须保持怎样的联系频率。
paragraphs.en: In an additional original scene, after a fictional gathering, someone wants to post a group photo in a small chat. Agreeing to be photographed, letting a friend keep it and allowing group members to see it are different decisions. Frequent photo exchanges do not settle permission for this image and audience. A refusal cannot be overridden by the mean. This concerns specific choices rather than prescribing a frequency of contact between friends.

title.en: State one specific permission or contact preference
title.zh: 说清一项具体的同意范围或联系偏好

paragraphs.zh: “这张照片可以发到这个群吗？如果不愿意，我就不发。”可以只用虚构照片练习说明具体内容与接收范围，不用真的上传、索取截图或解释不愿公开的全部理由。同意一次也不代表以后都同意。
paragraphs.en: “May I post this photo in this group? If you would rather not, I will not post it.” Practise naming the content and audience with an invented photo, without uploading anything, requesting screenshots or explaining every reason for privacy. Permission once does not mean permission for every later occasion.

title.en: A small event can leave room for different preferences
title.zh: 筹备小活动可以容纳不同偏好

paragraphs.zh: 补充原创场景：两位虚构朋友想参加一次社区拼图活动。一人喜欢整理边框，另一人想先找图案，但这次整理边框的人也可能想换个做法。可以讨论哪种方法便于当前合作，不用把偏好固定成“计划者”与“创意者”。找到共同玩法不同于技能测验；兴趣相似也不能自动决定谁承担收尾。这里看差异能否被讨论，而不是证明两人科学互补。
paragraphs.en: In an additional original scene, two fictional friends join a community jigsaw activity. One likes sorting edge pieces; the other wants to find images, but the edge sorter may want a different approach this time. Discuss what supports this particular collaboration without fixing planner and creative identities. Finding a shared way to play is not a skills test; similar interests do not assign cleanup. This concerns discussing differences, rather than proving scientifically complementary people.

title.en: Try one optional arrangement with explicit roles
title.zh: 尝试一项可以选择的安排，并说清角色

paragraphs.zh: “这次你想先做哪部分？如果方法不同，实际影响是什么？”各给一个可以选择的分工，也保留一起做、换角色或不一起参加的可能。不要从指南标题推定朋友能力，也不要求为了欣赏差异而接受不愿承担的任务。
paragraphs.en: “Which part would you like to begin with this time? If our methods differ, what is the practical effect?” Offer optional roles while retaining joint work, switched roles or separate participation. A guide title does not determine the friend’s ability or require an unwanted task in order to appreciate differences.
